title: Multiplication by $d$ is finite flat of degree $d^{2g}$
statement:
Let $A$ be an abelian variety of dimension $g$ over a field $k$
and let $d\geq1$. Then $[d]:A\to A$ of [def-sc-mult-n] is
finite, flat and locally free of rank $d^{2g}$, with finite kernel
$A[d]$ of order $d^{2g}$.
(*Stacks Project, Groupoid Schemes, Lemma 39.9.8,
[Tag 0BFG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BFG); Proposition
39.9.11, [Tag 03RP](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03RP)*.)

proof.text: By [lem-sc-mult-n-isogeny], $[d]:A\to A$ is a surjective homomorphism with finite kernel $A[d]$. Thus it is an isogeny by [def-sc-isogeny].

Put $r=\dim_k\Gamma(A[d],\mathcal O_{A[d]})$, the order of the finite kernel. Apply [lem-sc-isogeny-degree] to the isogeny of step 1: $[d]$ is finite flat and $[d]_*\mathcal O_A$ is locally free of rank $r$; its finite-morphism degree is $r$.

source.place: Groupoid Schemes, Lemma Tag 0BFG (label lemma-degree-multiplication-by-d), proof: finite flatness

proof.text: By [lem-sc-abelian-variety-projective] choose an ample invertible module $\mathcal L$ on $A$. The symmetric module $\mathcal N=\mathcal L\otimes[-1]^*\mathcal L$ is ample by [lem-sc-ample-tensor], and [lem-sc-mult-n-pullback] gives $[d]^*\mathcal N\cong\mathcal N^{\otimes d^2}$.

source.place: Groupoid Schemes, Lemma Tag 0BFG (label lemma-degree-multiplication-by-d), proof: symmetric ample module

proof.text: Write $P(m)=\chi(A,\mathcal N^{\otimes m})$. By [lem-sc-hilbert-polynomial] and [def-sc-hilbert-degree], its leading coefficient times $g!$ is $\deg_{\mathcal N}(A)$. The Hilbert polynomial for $\mathcal N^{\otimes d^2}$ is $P(d^2m)$; substituting $d^2m$ multiplies its degree-$g$ coefficient by $d^{2g}$. Therefore $\deg_{\mathcal N^{\otimes d^2}}(A)=d^{2g}\deg_{\mathcal N}(A)$.

source.place: Groupoid Schemes, Lemma Tag 0BFG (label lemma-degree-multiplication-by-d), final paragraph: Hilbert polynomial substitution

proof.text: By [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization], $A$ is a proper integral variety, so [lem-sc-deg-pullback-finite] applies to the finite surjective map of steps 1-2: $\deg_{[d]^*\mathcal N}(A)=r\deg_{\mathcal N}(A)$, using step 2's identification of the finite-morphism degree with $r$. Step 3 identifies its left side with $\deg_{\mathcal N^{\otimes d^2}}(A)$, which step 4 computes as $d^{2g}\deg_{\mathcal N}(A)$. Since [lem-sc-positive-ample-hilbert-degree] gives $\deg_{\mathcal N}(A)>0$, cancellation yields $r=d^{2g}$. Substitute this value into step 2: $[d]$ has the asserted locally free rank, and its finite kernel has the asserted order.
